For each part let E be the direction space of its affine base hull. Its compact convex hull has a relative interior in its translate of E, and the radius-1/4 ball has a relative interior in E-perp. Their Minkowski sum is full-dimensional in R^3. Its intersection with the old affine hull is exactly the old hull, since a vector in both E and E-perp must be zero.

For F, the affine hull is y+z=2. At an integer point off it, |y+z−2| is at least one, so the distance is at least 1/√2. For the line through 0 and 2e₁, a nonzero integer y or z gives distance at least one. For each singleton, a different lattice point has Euclidean distance at least one. Each lower bound exceeds 1/4, so no integer base is added.

The unit interval product is full-dimensional in R^3×R and gives ordinary auxiliary fiber volume one at each old site. The affine height x/2 on F extends to the whole base, and all other displayed heights are constant and likewise extend. Applying (p,u)↦(p,b_part(p)) gives exactly the required unit atoms while preserving the original bases.

overlap.comparison: Its canonical lift can add integer coordinates and change affine rank while preserving occupied parities. The present obstruction fixes the original base coordinates within every positive affine pushforward, a different allocation class.

Its cost-eight versus four example restricts minors to support-roof contact faces of a positive triangular family. The current class permits arbitrary positive affine-graph decompositions, including fractional allocations, and obtains nine versus eight for a hollow atomic law.
